Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 6

The rule is written on docs/testbench.md 'Sessions and the loopback server' in e95c6c099: debian:trixie-slim pinned by digest, openssh-server pinned by version, sshd -i under podman --network=none --pull=never via sg, loud failure without podman, and the SELinux probe removed. ### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `ac6fe50b7fbccf059e7168adc46095ad` · 2026-09-30T23:21:48Z

> Checked 2026-09-30: bench-ssh-loopback-openssh is the ONLY SELinux failure in the whole bench (K10's run: 243 PASS, 1 FAIL). Every case against Redoubt's own sshd passes (bench-ssh-loopback*, sshd-loopback-*). Cause, as docs/todo/ssh-loopback-host.md says: Wash runs as a system service, so every member and the bench run in system_u:system_r:unconfined_service_t; the reference case starts the host's OpenSSH sshd in inetd mode, which with SELinux enforcing moves the login shell to unconfined_u:unconfined_r:unconfined_t, a transition the service context may not make, so /bin/bash: Permission denied. The case exists on purpose, as the session runner's independent witness (a runner bug shared with our sshd would pass every self-check). podman and docker are installed; the Dockerfile's dev image exists.

### Orchestrator · Owner decision requested

Event: `8660fdc1c81591bfe2befcf89ff5df01` · 2026-09-30T23:21:56Z

> The OpenSSH reference case and SELinux
> 
> 1. You're right: the only SELinux failure is bench-ssh-loopback-openssh, the case that runs the host's OpenSSH sshd. Every case against our own sshd passes. It fails because Wash runs as a system service (unconfined_service_t), and OpenSSH moves the login shell into unconfined_t, which that context may not do. The case is deliberately the session runner's independent witness: it's the only thing that would catch a runner bug our sshd shares. What should we do?
>    - Run OpenSSH's sshd in a container (recommended): Recommended. The reference case starts OpenSSH's sshd -i inside podman (a small image, or the Dockerfile's). A container sees SELinux as disabled, so there's no login-context transition. The witness stays real, and no host policy or service change is needed. One bench package (Tier A, bench), S-M.
>    - A local SELinux policy module: You install a module that lets unconfined_service_t transition to unconfined_t for sshd's shell (root, host-only). No code change, but it widens what every Wash service process may do.
>    - Drop the reference case: Delete it and the todo page. The runner's self-checks run only against our own sshd, with no independent witness: a weaker bench claim, stated as a residual.
>    - Leave it as is: Keep failing it loudly and skipping it with --allow-skip, as now.

> The rule is written and committed on redoubt as e95c6c099 (docs/testbench.md "Sessions and the loopback server"; the todo page's Done-when is updated; the docs case passes). The SSH2 brief is ready: .wash/local/SSH2-implementer.md, with the container as its own first step. Base e95c6c099, size L. The plan node body is updated.

> Decision refs to attach when you resolve (a reply cannot carry them): d44dbb71458b03edd47131355487ca91 (the owner's answer) and e95c6c099.
> 
> Rulings:
> - Image: tests/ssh-reference/Containerfile. debian:trixie-slim pinned by digest, openssh-server pinned by version; not the dev Dockerfile (it uses `latest` and is huge). Tagged by a hash of the file and built only when missing.
> - Runner: the ProxyCommand runs `podman run -i --rm --network=none --pull=never`, with the case directory mounted `:z` (shared label, so concurrent sessions can append to one log), and `sshd -i` in the container. It logs in only root, which is the bench's user outside.
> - The witness: the case keeps every step it has, and the probe requires OpenSSH's version in the server's log.
> - No podman or image: the OpenSSH cases fail loudly, as a named host lack, and are skipped only under --allow-skip.
> - The SELinux probe branch and its test go, and ssh-loopback-host.md is deleted in the package.
> 
> Checked here: plain `podman run` fails from Wash's service context. The service's primary group is root, and newuidmap refuses to map. `sg mick -c 'podman run ...'` works, and pulls work. The runner starts podman under sg with the user's primary group, taken from passwd rather than written in. Docker is no fallback (its socket needs the docker group). Inside the dev container the case becomes a named skip.
